data.title: Checkout
data.description: How shoppers place an order — guest flows, address, delivery date, payment methods, and WhatsApp ordering.

children.text: The checkout page is where a shopper reviews their cart, enters a delivery address, picks a payment method, and places an order. The exact steps a shopper sees depend on which checkout settings your store has enabled in the CloudPos admin.
from their cart. What happens next depends on your settings:

content.text: Delivery address form, order summary, and a "Place Order" button
Redirected to the sign-in page; checkout is only accessible after logging in

A phone-number entry screen followed by a one-time code before the address form
An OTP verification gate, then the order is sent to the store's WhatsApp with a prefilled order summary

children.text: Guest checkout in CloudPos Ecom is not truly anonymous. When a guest verifies their phone via OTP, a customer account is created automatically in the background — they just never set a password. If CHECKOUT
ACCOUNT is also ON, the shopper is invited to set a password after the order is confirmed.
When a guest visits checkout, the store checks settings in this order:
— if ON, redirect to login immediately (no checkout UI is shown).
— if ON, show the "Have an account? Sign in for faster checkout" gate. Tapping "Continue with phone" leads to OTP entry.
— if either is ON, show the phone + OTP verification screen.
Otherwise, the guest proceeds straight to the address and payment form.

data.description: How the storefront supports multiple languages, locale-prefixed URLs, and right-to-left (RTL) layout.

children.text: CloudPos Ecom supports multiple languages per store. Shoppers switch languages using the language switcher in the navbar. The storefront automatically adapts its layout direction for right-to-left (RTL) languages such as Arabic.
The platform currently ships two languages:
Adding a new language requires adding a locale entry to
and a corresponding dictionary file under
. Contact your implementation team to add a new locale.
that is prefixless in the URL — it does not appear as a path segment. Additional locales are prefixed with their language code:

Shoppers browsing in the default language see clean, short URLs. Switching to a non-default language adds the locale code as the first URL segment; switching back removes it. All page URLs remain in sync — switching language on a product page stays on that product page, just in the new language.
The navbar includes a language switcher that lists the locales enabled for the store. Tapping a language:
Rewrites the current page URL to add or remove the locale prefix.
Navigates to that URL, reloading the page in the selected language.
Static UI text — buttons, labels, navigation links, error messages — switches immediately from the built-in translation dictionary for that language.
Dynamic content — product names, category names, product descriptions — is translated by the backend and served in the selected language automatically.
When a shopper selects Arabic, the entire page layout direction flips to
Flex and grid flow directions (items flow from right to left)
The direction is set at the HTML root element, so all standard UI elements adapt automatically with no per-component changes required.
Which languages does my store show?

children.text: Set it once on the Worker and never hardcode it:

content.code: wrangler secret put REVALIDATE_SECRET

children.text: The ERP stores the same value and sends it on every
call. There is one shared secret across all tenants — the
field (or the request Host) determines which tenant is purged; the secret only proves the caller is authorized. If the secret is lost, set a new one with
and update the ERP config to match.
For one-off purges, testing, and recovery, use the PowerShell script from the project root:

content.code:
# Full purge — all 10 tenants
./scripts/revalidate.ps1

# One tenant, full purge
./scripts/revalidate.ps1 -Tenant giftat

# Products only, all tenants (e.g. after a bulk price import)
./scripts/revalidate.ps1 -Category products

# Settings only, one tenant
./scripts/revalidate.ps1 -Tenant giftat -Category settings

# Override origin and pass secret inline
./scripts/revalidate.ps1 -Secret <value> -Origin https://giftat.in

children.text: Set the secret as an environment variable to keep it out of shell history:

content.code: $env:REVALIDATE_SECRET = ""
